key_insight: Symmetry-preserving variational circuits achieve accurate lattice Gross–Neveu energies, while transferred adaptive circuits extend one-flavor evaluations to 400 qubits without target-side optimization.
engineering_relevance: At fixed flavor number, range caps, and append count, the adaptive construction offers linear precompilation local-factor scaling with volume and a volume-independent shared-parameter count.
method: Build fixed circuits conserving total fermion number or each flavor number.
Use SC-ADAPT-VQE with bulk, boundary-sensitive, and cross-flavor generators.
Prepare sector-resolved excited states by sequential deflation and assess degenerate eigenspaces using projector fidelities.
evidence_signal: Classical benchmarks through 30 qubits report selected massive fixed-circuit relative energy errors of approximately 10⁻⁵–2×10⁻⁴; one-flavor MPS evaluations at 60–400 qubits show approximately 0.35%–1.76% deviations from DMRG references.
watch_item: Fixed-accuracy scaling to arbitrary volumes remains unestablished, and the reported benchmarks are classical circuit evaluations rather than quantum-hardware demonstrations.
paper_title: Symmetry-Preserving and Scalable Variational Circuits for the Lattice Gross-Neveu Model
